Compute the electrical resistivity of a wire with length 0.492 m and diameter 1.944 mm.
The wire has an electrical resistance of 11.705 Ω.
Use A = πd² for the circular cross-sectional area, with d = 1.944e-3 m.
Calculate the cross-sectional area A = π × (1.944e-3)² = 1.1872e-5 m².
Calculate the resistivity using ρ = R·A / L.
Substituting values: ρ = 11.705 × 1.1872e-5 / 0.492.
The result is ρ ≈ 2.824e-4 Ω·m.
